page: Microsoft Azure EC96ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at two threads per core. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 flags are absent.

The configuration provides 672.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 7.0 GB per vCPU core. In addition to system memory, the instance is equipped with 3865 GB of bundled local solid-state drive (SSD) storage for high-speed scratch space and temporary file operations. No hardware GPU accelerators are attached to this instance profile.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong parallel execution, with stress-ng multi-core performance reaching 108196.57, placing it in the top 25th percentile of tested systems, alongside a stress-ng single-core score of 2333.57. Memory and caching subsystems demonstrate high throughput, recording 91.13 million operations per second in redis SET benchmarks. While the absence of AVX-512 restricts certain advanced vectorized floating-point calculations, the platform provides strong resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for distributed caching tiers, in-memory databases, and large-scale data transformation pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure EC96ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core, alongside 672.0 GB of system memory (7.0 GB per core). Bundled local storage includes 3865 GB of SSD capacity, while GPU hardware is omitted. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates moderate single-core throughput with a stress-ng score of 2333.57, paired with upper-quartile multi-core capability at 108196.57. Redis SET benchmarks reach 91.13 million operations per second, confirming strong memory data transfer rates. While lacking AVX-512 extensions, its combination of high core counts, substantial RAM, and fast local SSD storage delivers balanced resource density for large-scale in-memory databases, caching tiers, enterprise analytics, and high-throughput data processing tasks.
